problem_statement: A projectile is launched from ground level with speed u = 40.0 m/s at an angle theta = 30.0 degrees above the horizontal. Taking downward gravity g = 10.0 m/s^2, calculate: (a) the time of flight T, (b) the maximum height H, (c) the horizontal range R, and (d) the velocity of the projectile at the apex.
target_quantity: Time of flight T, maximum height H, horizontal range R, apex velocity vector v_apex
governing_principles: Independence of horizontal motion (u_x = const) and vertical motion under gravity (a_y = -g)
solution_strategy: Decompose initial velocity into horizontal and vertical components. Apply 1D vertical kinematics for T and H, and horizontal motion for R. At apex, vertical velocity vanishes.

ordered_steps.equation_latex: u_x = u\cos\theta = 40.0 \cos 30^\circ = 40.0 \left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 20\sqrt{3} \approx 34.64\text{ m/s}, \quad u_y = u\sin\theta = 40.0 \sin 30^\circ = 20.0\text{ m/s}

ordered_steps.action_description: Calculate time of flight T using T = 2 u_y / g
Calculate maximum height H using H = u_y^2 / (2g)
ordered_steps.justification: Apex condition v_y = 0 in v_y^2 = u_y^2 - 2gH.

ordered_steps.action_description: Calculate horizontal range R using R = u_x T
ordered_steps.justification: Uniform horizontal motion x = u_x t.
At the apex, v_y = 0 while horizontal velocity u_x remains unaltered.
ordered_steps.calculation_details: Speed at apex is 20 sqrt(3) m/s directed horizontally.

final_answer: (a) Time of flight T = 4.0 s; (b) Maximum height H = 20.0 m; (c) Horizontal range R = 80*sqrt(3) m (approx 138.56 m); (d) Velocity at apex = 20*sqrt(3) i m/s (approx 34.64 m/s horizontal).
sanity_checks: Using range formula R = u^2 sin(2 theta)/g = (1600 * sin 60 deg)/10 = 160 * (sqrt(3)/2) = 80 sqrt(3) m, perfect agreement.
Apex speed is non-zero (34.64 m/s) and strictly equal to horizontal component.
trap_alerts: Do not assume velocity at apex is zero! Only the vertical component v_y is zero; horizontal speed u_x persists.
